item.title: Republicans Let Trump Keep Unparalleled Benefit: I.R.S. Immunity
item.description: The rebellion against Todd Blanche’s nomination to be attorney general, now seemingly contained, at no point fundamentally questioned President Trump’s new protections from the I.R.S.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump no longer has to worry about the Internal Revenue Service coming after him for any of the many aggressive tax positions he has taken over the years.

item.title: Pirro Meets With Trump at the White House After He Said She ‘Choked’ in Reflecting Pool Case
item.description: President Trump said Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., “folded like an umbrella.” For now, her job appeared to be safe, according to two people familiar with the meeting.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green, Katie Rogers, Tyler Pager and Maggie Haberman
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump on Monday in the Oval Office, where he grew angry when asked whether he had spoken with Jeanine Pirro about her decision to withdraw a felony charge against a former Olympic canoeist.

item.title: An Emerging Deal Between Iran and Oman to Reopen Hormuz Would Come at a Cost for Trump
item.description: The deal would address President Trump’s most urgent political problem by allowing ships to move again. But it would give Iran strategic leverage it did not have before the war.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger, Farnaz Fassihi and Eric Schmitt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Reuters
item.media:description: Ships in the Strait of Hormuz seen from Musandam, Oman, in June. An emerging deal, if it happens, would reopen shipping traffic in the strait, according to Iranian and U.S. officials.

item.title: Sailors Working in Strait of Hormuz Are Caught in Crossfire of Iran War
item.description: Thousands of civilian workers remain stranded on ships at risk of attack by Iran. On one vessel, sailors have been held by the Iranian navy for more than three months.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross and Peter Eavis
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Tomas Munita for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S.-Israel attacks against Iran on Feb. 28 followed by Iran’s almost-immediate closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has stranded thousands of sailors.

item.title: A Currency Trader at Heart, Bessent Bets on Japan’s Yen
item.description: Coordinated intervention allowed Japan to support its currency without selling off its U.S. debt holdings.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, last week returned to his roots as a hedge fund manager in making a currency bet to help stabilize Japan’s currency.

item.title: Author of Democrats’ 2024 Autopsy Says Party Left Out Key Chapter
item.description: A dispute over the chapter between the author and the Democratic National Committee has added to the party’s turmoil as it tries to look forward, not backward.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Kent Nishimura for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Democratic National Committee’s autopsy of the 2024 election was meant to examine missteps that led to the party’s defeat.

item.title: Inside the Democratic Socialists of America Summit
item.description: Our politics reporter Kellen Browning went to the Democratic Socialists of America’s national summit in Chicago to learn more about the group’s new platform.
item.dc:creator: Kellen Browning, Christina Shaman, Nour Idriss, Jon Hazell, Rafaela Balster and Jamie Kelter Davis

item.title: In Michigan’s 7th District’s Democratic Primary, a Centrist Split Boosts Progressive Hopes
item.description: Unable to unite behind a single candidate in Michigan’s Seventh Congressional District, moderate Democrats worry that they’ve complicated their chances in a key November battleground.
item.dc:creator: Evan Gorelick
item.media:credit: Matt Maasdam For Congress; Nathan Layne/Reuters; William Lawrence for U.S. Congress

item.title: Trump, Graham Dominate Senate Race: 5 Takeaways from South Carolina Debate.
item.description: The legacy of Lindsey Graham loomed over the field to replace him in a debate Monday. All eyes were on his sister, Darline, who was endorsed by President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times

item.title: Cambridge Professor’s Jason Arday’s Work Challenged Ahead of Book Launch
item.description: A knife-wielding masked man. A pig’s head outside his parents’ door. Running 30 marathons in 35 days. The Cambridge professor Jason Arday, accused of plagiarism, says he’s been through it all. Not everyone believes him.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler and Alexandra Alter
item.media:credit: via Simon & Schuster; Photo by Anselm Ebulue

item.title: Immigrant Held at Delaney Detention Center Has Died, Officials Say
item.description: The mayor of Newark identified the dead man as Edwin Lopez-Cornejo. The New Jersey center has been the focus of intense scrutiny for its treatment of detainees.
item.dc:creator: Ana Ley, Tracey Tully and Mark Bonamo
item.media:credit: Madison Swart for The New York Times
item.media:description: A man held at the Delaney Hall detention center in Newark died over the weekend.

item.title: U.S. Sends Flight With Deportees to Venezuela for First Time Since Earthquakes
item.description: A plane with 147 Venezuelans landed on Monday in the South American country amid criticism over the deaths of deportees housed in a collapsed building during June’s quakes.
item.dc:creator: Genevieve Glatsky
item.media:credit: Alejandro Cegarra for The New York Times
item.media:description: A Venezuelan-operated plane arrived with deported migrants at Simón Bolívar International Airport in Maiquetía, Venezuela, in December.

item.title: N.Y. Law Barring ICE Agents From Wearing Masks Is Blocked by Judge
item.description: While the ruling dealt a blow to New York’s efforts to rein in ICE, a ban on formal cooperation with local police officers will move forward.
item.dc:creator: Grace Ashford
item.media:credit: Madison Swart for The New York Times
item.media:description: Agents working for ICE typically wear face coverings, making it difficult to identify them in cases where they may have overstepped their authority.

item.title: Spotlight on Fauci Said to Boost Book Sales for Kennedy and His Publisher
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., his son, and Senator Rand Paul have all written books criticizing Dr. Anthony S. Fauci. All were published by a company led by a close Kennedy adviser.
item.dc:creator: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., now the health secretary, published “The Real Anthony Fauci” in 2021.

item.title: Andy Burnham’s First Weeks as UK Prime Minister: TikToks, Podcasts and Promises
item.description: Andy Burnham’s social media push appears to be resonating with some voters. But he faces big decisions about how to pay for his promises.
item.dc:creator: Michael D. Shear
item.media:credit: Pool photo by Temilade Adelaja
item.media:description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, center, visiting an Alstom training center as he unveiled new technical educational routes aimed at tackling youth unemployment, in Derby, England, in July.

item.title: ‘A War Zone’: Spokane Wildfires Leave a Devastating Trail of Destruction
item.description: Despite the scale of the damage, there have been no reported fatalities in the fires that started over the weekend. Late on Monday, officials arrested a man suspected of setting one of the fires.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: Residents returned to survey damage left in the wildfires in Spokane, Wash.

item.title: Man Arrested on Suspicion of Arson in Spokane Wildfire
item.description: Aaron Farinacci, 37, was arrested after a witness reported seeing him kneeling near the ignition site of a major fire in Washington State, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.media:credit: Loren Elliott for The New York Times
item.media:description: Destruction left in the wake of the Old Trails fire in Spokane, Wash.

item.title: New Zealand Has Ended Greyhound Racing. Now It Has to Manage the Aftermath.
item.description: As the country holds its final greyhound race, the government has committed to finding homes for dogs and supporting people whose livelihoods depended on racing.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Stoakes and Tatsiana Chypsanava
item.category: Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals
item.media:credit: Tatsiana Chypsanava for The New York Times
item.media:description: The transition will be funded by New Zealand’s state-regulated national betting agency. Much of that money will be spent on rehoming about 1,400 greyhounds.

item.title: Gen Z Can’t Afford a First Date
item.description: From $130 dinners to expensive cocktails and even exorbitant movie tickets, a crushing economy in New York City is creating a fresh barrier to love.
item.dc:creator: Troy Closson
item.media:credit: Gary Hershorn/Getty Images
item.media:description: People in their 20s and 30s are dating less than earlier generations did. The high cost of going out is one of the reasons.
